front.title: Mapping YANG Models and Instance Data to TM Forum Data Models and APIs

abstract.t: This document describes a mapping between YANG models/instance data and TM Forum Open API Data Models. It covers both service-facing and resource-facing APIs and their catalog specifications, showing how YANG-defined structures can be represented as TMF Characteristics and CharacteristicSpecifications. The document also outlines approaches for handling nested YANG containers and lists, and provides implementation guidelines that align YANG attributes with TMF constructs without prescribing a single mapping method.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Service providers commonly use OSS systems with NETCONF/YANG interfaces (e.g., YANG models ) to describe configuration and operational state for network and service resources, while TM Forum Open APIs are increasingly used by BSS systems to order and manage services and resources. These two ecosystems define different data models and interaction styles for overlapping concepts, which can lead to duplicated modeling effort and inconsistent behavior across interfaces.

This document specifies a mapping between YANG models/instance data and TM Forum data models and APIs, with the goal of enabling consistent representation of resources and services across management interfaces. The mapping is intended to facilitate translation between YANG-defined structures and TM Forum resource/service constructs, while preserving semantics such as hierarchy, identity, and constraints.
The mapping applies to YANG models in general and is particularly relevant to IETF service and network models such as the L3SM , L3NM , L2SM , and L2NM .

The scope of this document is limited to the mapping model and the associated transformation rules. It does not define new protocols, nor does it mandate a specific implementation architecture. Operational concerns such as service orchestration workflows and business processes are out of scope, except where they affect the interpretation of the mapped data.

section.name: Where the TMF Mapping Fits
section.t: The framework in separates service, network, and device layers. The TMF interfaces addressed by this document typically sit at the product or service boundary (customer or OSS/BSS-facing), while YANG models and controllers span service, network, and device layers. The mapping defined here is intended to bridge those boundaries, enabling service and resource definitions to be expressed consistently across TMF Open APIs and YANG-based automation.

section.name: YANG Instance Data in TMF Configuration and Ordering APIs
section.t: In the Ordering/Activation and Configuration APIs, ordering is expressed through ServiceOrder and ServiceOrderItem in TMF640 and TMF641 , and through ResourceOrder and ResourceOrderItem in TMF652 and TMF702 . In these APIs, the parameterization of a Service or Resource is conveyed primarily through serviceCharacteristic or resourceCharacteristic entries, each with a name, a value, and (where applicable) a valueType.

YANG instance data MUST be mapped into this Characteristic structure in a manner that preserves the meaning of the source data. Leaf and leaf-list values SHOULD be represented as individual Characteristic entries (service or resource as appropriate). The Characteristic name SHOULD be derived from the YANG node identifier (or path, when required for disambiguation), and the Characteristic value MUST reflect the YANG-typed value using an appropriate encoding. Where YANG defines units or enumerations, the resulting Characteristic values SHOULD be encoded consistently so that the receiver can interpret them without additional schema inference.

Containers and lists introduce structure beyond a single value. Their mapping into Characteristics is described in the following sections and can require decomposition, flattening, or structured value representations depending on the chosen approach.

section.name: YANG Models in TMF Catalog APIs
section.t: TMF633 defines the Service Catalog model, where a ServiceSpecification captures the design-time description of a service and its allowed parameters. Parameter definitions are expressed as serviceSpecCharacteristic entries, each of which can include one or more serviceSpecCharacteristicValue entries to constrain allowed values.

TMF634 defines the Resource Catalog model in a parallel fashion. A ResourceSpecification carries resourceSpecCharacteristic entries and their associated resourceSpecCharacteristicValue constraints, mirroring the service catalog structure.

A YANG schema SHOULD be mapped to a corresponding Service or Resource Specification such that each relevant YANG leaf or leaf-list becomes a Characteristic specification entry. The Characteristic definition SHOULD include the expected value type and, where applicable, the permitted set of values. Enumerations and identityrefs SHOULD be mapped to discrete Characteristic value entries, while ranges and patterns SHOULD be reflected in the Characteristic constraints. YANG min-elements and max-elements statements SHOULD inform the Characteristic cardinality where the TMF model supports it.

This mapping ensures that catalog-level specifications align with the instance-level Characteristics used in TMF640/TMF641 and TMF652/TMF702, enabling consistent validation of service or resource orders against the intended YANG-defined model.

section.name: Mapping YANG leafs and leaf-lists to TMF Characteristics
section.t: YANG leafs and leaf-lists represent the fundamental data elements in a YANG model. When mapping these constructs to TMF Characteristics, each leaf or leaf-list SHOULD be represented as a separate Characteristic entry within the corresponding Service or Resource instance.

ul.li: The Characteristic name SHOULD be derived from the YANG node identifier.
The Characteristic value MUST be encoded according to the YANG type.
For leaf-lists, the Characteristic value SHOULD be represented as an array, and the valueType SHOULD indicate the array nature (e.g., stringArray, integerArray).

Map YANG types as follows: boolean to boolean, string to string, integer types to integer, decimal64 to number, and enumeration to string. For enumerations, the allowed values SHOULD be constrained using the TMF characteristic value list (e.g., serviceSpecCharacteristicValue or resourceSpecCharacteristicValue) so the instance Characteristic value is validated against the catalog-defined set.
Set minCardinality to 1 for key or mandatory leaves; otherwise set it to 0.
Use maxCardinality of 1 for leaves and the YANG max-elements value for leaf-lists.
Map YANG string patterns to the Characteristic regex field.
Express YANG defaults as Characteristic default value specifications for TMF633/634.

section.name: Mapping Approaches for YANG containers and lists
section.t: YANG models commonly represent complex data structures by composing containers, lists, leafs, and leaf-lists into YANG data trees that capture hierarchy, optionality, and repeated elements. Mapping those constructs into TM Forum Service and Resource Data Models can be approached in several ways, each with different trade-offs in expressiveness, Catalog behavior, and operational clarity. This section enumerates four approaches that may be applied.

section.name: Approach 1: Complex Characteristics
section.t: The structure can be embedded in a single Characteristic by using the TM Forum "Any" value type. In this case, the concrete schema of the value MUST be provided out-of-band, typically as a JSON Schema artifact. This preserves structure, but it introduces an additional schema dependency and shifts validation responsibility to implementers.

section.name: Approach 2: Decomposition into Services/Resources
section.t: Each data tree layer can be mapped to its own TM Forum Service or Resource, linked through supportingService or corresponding Resource relationships. This enables explicit decomposition and reuse; however, it causes each layer to appear in the Service Catalog or Resource Catalog as a separately orderable item. Implementations would then need to expose and manage the appropriate relationships (e.g., parent-child, requires), and the resulting granularity can become too fine to be operationally meaningful.

section.name: Approach 3: Decomposition into Features
section.t: Each data tree layer can be represented as a TM Forum Service Feature or Resource Feature within an enclosing Service or Resource. This keeps Catalog entries stable, but the current TM Forum model does not define feature nesting (i.e., there is no supportingFeature-like construct). Implementations could introduce a controlled extension (e.g., via a schemaLocation extension) to represent feature hierarchy, but such nesting SHOULD be standardized in a future TM Forum Open API release for maximum interoperability.

section.name: Approach 4: Encode Schema in Characteristic Names
section.t: The structure can be flattened by encoding path-like information in Characteristic names (e.g., a YANG path fragment). This is simple to implement but it cannot represent cardinality accurately and tends to obscure the original YANG data tree, making validation and processing ambiguous.

section.name: Implementation Guidelines
section.t: This section summarizes a practical mapping between common YANG attributes and TMF constructs in both the Catalog and Ordering/Activation APIs. The guidelines are based on experience gathered from a Proof of Concept implementation.

An implementation MAY support the ability to map an entire YANG schema into a TMF Service or Resource Specification or it MAY allow the operator to specify a subtree of the YANG schema that will be mapped to a particular Service or Resource Specification. In either case, the mapping process MUST preserve the semantics of the YANG model, including data types, constraints, and hierarchical relationships starting from the mapped subtree.

To indicate the part of the YANG schema that is mapped to a particular TMF Service or Resource Specification, an implementation MAY use a YANG extension (e.g., tmf-cfs) to annotate the relevant YANG node with a reference to the corresponding TMF Specification (e.g., tmf-cfs="TMF633:ServiceSpec123").

An implementation MAY use YANG extension to indicate which parts of a YANG tree are mapped into TMF according to a particular method as described in the previous section. For example, a tmf-mapping extension could be used to specify whether a container is mapped as a complex Characteristic, as a separate Service/Resource, or as a Feature.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This memo includes no request to IANA.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This document defines a mapping between YANG models/instance data and TM Forum data models and APIs. The mapping itself introduces no new protocol elements, but it can affect how existing security properties are preserved when translating data between representations.

Implementations of this mapping MUST preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and authorization semantics of the source model. In particular, access control decisions tied to YANG nodes (including read, write, and notification permissions) MUST be enforced equivalently on the mapped TM Forum resources and operations. Failing to do so can result in privilege escalation or unintended disclosure.

When mapping data across administrative or trust boundaries, operators MUST ensure that transport security (e.g., TLS) and mutual authentication are used as appropriate for the deployed APIs. The mapping process MUST NOT bypass auditing, logging, or rate-limiting controls that are required for the underlying interfaces.

Finally, any reference data used by the mapping (such as schema registries, profiles, or transformation rules) SHOULD be protected from unauthorized modification, as tampering could lead to incorrect data interpretation or security policy violations.
